title: First experiment with local generative models
author: zjgkkn
selftext:
Everything you see in the video was generated locally on a laptop with an RTX 3070, in a single night, on the first try. The only things I regenerated were models that came out clearly broken.

Then Claude assembled it all into a demo level in Unity.

Assets Studio tool: [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/assets\_studio](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/assets_studio)

comments.author: i_rate_slop
comments.body: I can only imagine this was downvoted by someone making an asset studio tool as a product. I think it's awesome that you open sourced it.

comments.author: SilkieBug
comments.body: What did you use to generate the 3d models, Pixal3d in ComfyUI?

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body:
I started with a FLUX + TripoSR + Make It Animatable (for rigging) pipeline, and some of that may have ended up in the video. But then I switched to Qwen Image -> Hunyuan3D -> Hunyuan Paint. Everything is heavily quantized to fit into 8 GiB of VRAM, but it's the clear winner out of everything I managed to run on a 3070.  
  
On top of that, there's a small job queue, a library, and a Python UI: [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/assets\_studio](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/assets_studio)

replies.author: Shuma665
replies.body:
Thanks it looks great thanks for sharing you models and toolset. I'll check out the repo later. 
I made 'We got meshy at home" and I can models things on my 4070 12gb but I didn't find them very suitable for animation so I'm curious what you are doing there

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body: Thanks! Honestly, I don't have a real solution for animation either. Right now I use Make It Animatable plus Mixamo animation packs, but that only works for humanoid models without extra parts like capes, tails, etc. Finding something that handles rigging/animation as well as the other modalities would be really cool.

replies.author: Shuma665
replies.body: Astra and 6.1 sol have been doing an ok job for me doing the actual animating and rigging it's more the faces from the generated mesh were not very conducive.  I've been building from scratch using a common base character and then doing a modified gauntlet loop but it's been slower than I'd care for.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body:
And they will be if GPU pricing ever goes back to sane levels.

The MSRP on a 5090 is like $2000. You can't find one for anything less than $5k.

replies.author: Qinistral
replies.body:
How many tripo3d models can I make for 5k? 
Maybe 5k-10k depending on detail etc?

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body:
I'm not sure. But yea, right now the cost is too high for anyone except someone doing this shit as business and churning out tons of stuff. Like I was debating getting one for local video gen, then I did the math and realized if I do a Modal instance and run video gen up there, a 15 second clip costs like $0.25. That's a *very long time* to break even.

That said, Modal is pretty good if you can figure out how to tap your workflow into their GPU renting. It's anywhere from $2-$7/hr of *active* GPU time (you don't pay while it's idle). And, right now at least, they give you $30/month in credit on the free tier.

It becomes expensive if you're constantly using GPU, but if you're doing spot gens, it can be pretty cost efficient.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: If you don't get textures from them, you can get \~250 Smart mesh models for $20 with a new account. If you go with standard meshes and use some pipeline to retopo them, you can get 3x that for $20. Textures I think half the number. So for 5k you could get around \~125k models, give or take. Also each one of those comes in packs of 4 since there isn't a good reason to generate less than that. But yes, you're better off just paying them in most cases (although that doesn't account for other combined uses of the card.)

replies.author: AlgaeNo3373
replies.body:
The costs to entry are already business-scaled at top-end, where a card costs roughly same as someone's yearly salary (30k), so it's already priced as labour replacement more than prosumer tool.

But it's interesting OP is doing this with a more basic card. That's quite encouraging!

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body: So what did you do about the dense mesh topology you typically get with generative 3D models? Did Claude handle that?

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body: Yes, it did. By reducing polygon budgets and by introducing Unity's level of detail. Joints deform worse up close, btw.

comments.author: retrorays
comments.body: sorry I dont get it - what did claude do vs. your local models?

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body:
Claude wrote the code for the studio and the model servers. It also wrote the prompts for everything: the images that were then turned into 3D assets, the sound effects, and the soundtrack. Animations come from Mixamo.

The local models do the actual generation for each modality: text-to-image, image-to-3D, rigging, 3D painting (texturing), text-to-sound, text-to-speech, and text-to-music.
